verified_facts.fact: Eligibility: you can generally claim a DASP if you held a temporary visa (not subclass 405 or 410) while you built up super, that visa has expired or been cancelled, you have left Australia and hold no other active visa, and you are not an Australian or New Zealand citizen or a permanent resident.
The ATO says claiming through its online system is free and eligibility is confirmed automatically ('This is a free service and your eligibility is confirmed automatically').

How to apply: the ATO's DASP online application system handles super held by a fund and ATO-held super; you can start and save an application while still in Australia. Paper alternative: form NAT 7204, one to each fund. ATO-held super paper form: NAT 74880.

One application per account: when the online system finds super accounts (search needs your TFN, which is optional), it presents an application for each account found. If a fund is not found you start an application with the fund's ABN. The system shows statuses such as submitted, but not whether the fund has processed it; for that you contact the fund.

Tax: for working holiday makers (417 or 462) the taxed element and the untaxed element of the taxable component are both withheld at 65%; the tax-free component is nil. Other temporary residents: 35% taxed element, 45% untaxed element. Table captioned 'DASP tax rates (from 1 July 2017)'. If the DASP includes contributions made while on a 417 or 462 visa (or an associated bridging visa), the WHM rate applies to the entire payment.

Processing time as the ATO states it: 'Your DASP will generally be paid within 28 days of your completed application being received.' It can take longer if the application is incomplete or more documents are requested. For ATO-held super the ATO's service standard is 28 days from lodgement and it cannot always meet it.
verified_facts.note: Not 'within 28 days of approval'. Individual funds may state their own target (for example ART: aims to pay within 20 days of receiving the form and documents from the ATO); do not quote fund targets as general facts.

verified_facts.fact: Unclaimed super: if you do not apply, your fund transfers it to the ATO once at least 6 months have passed since you left Australia and your visa ceased to be in effect. You can still claim it as a DASP, at any time.
verified_facts.detail: Under the ATO's unclaimed super protocol the 6 months run from the later of the visa ceasing or the departure, and funds report and pay by the next scheduled statement day (31 October and 30 April each year), so the move can come later than 6 months.

verified_facts.fact: Finding your funds: the DASP online system (after eligibility, with your TFN), ATO online services via myGov linked to the ATO (Super, then Fund details; ATO-held super shows there; 'Contact fund' marks a lost member account), the ATO app, or by phone.

Identity: your super fund may require certified copies of proof of identity documents (online and paper). For paper applications with a balance of $5,000 or more you may need a Certification of Immigration Status from the Department of Home Affairs (form 1194), which has a fee; under $5,000 other evidence can be given, though a fund may still ask for the certificate.
A tax refund can only be paid into an Australian bank account ('We can only pay refunds into an Australian bank account').

A DASP can be paid to an overseas account where the fund offers it (fund dependent; for example Cbus pays by international telegraphic transfer and does not accept Revolut or Wise; ART accepts international bank details).
verified_facts.note: Not stated on the ATO DASP page; present it as 'depending on the fund', never as a general rule.

verified_facts.fact: New Zealand citizens cannot claim a DASP; super can in some cases be transferred to a KiwiSaver scheme (trans-Tasman retirement savings transfer).
verified_facts.checked: 2026-11-05 (linked from the ATO DASP page; NZ page itself not fetched)

S1_hero_answer_first.en_source_text: You claim it as a Departing Australia Superannuation Payment (DASP) once your 417 or 462 visa has expired or been cancelled and you have left Australia. You apply online with the ATO, free, or on a paper form to each fund. For working holiday makers 65% of the taxable component is withheld, and the rest can be paid to an overseas account if your fund offers it. What usually holds a claim up is a visa that still shows as active, a fund you did not know about, or identity documents a fund will not accept.

S3_how_to_claim_steps.en_heading: How do you claim your super after leaving Australia?
en_steps: Check that you can claim: your visa has expired or been cancelled, you have left Australia, and no other Australian visa is active. You can check your visa in VEVO.

Find every account: the ATO's DASP online application searches by your TFN, and myGov linked to the ATO lists every fund under Super, then Fund details, including super already transferred to the ATO.

Apply: the online application is free and creates one application per account; you can start and save it before you fly and submit it once you have left. The paper alternative is form NAT 7204, sent to each fund.

Prove your identity: a fund may ask for certified copies of your identity documents. On a paper application for $5,000 or more you may also need a Certification of Immigration Status from Home Affairs.

Get paid: 65% of the taxable component is withheld, and the ATO says the rest is generally paid within 28 days of a complete application, to an Australian account or, if your fund offers it, an overseas one.
S3_how_to_claim_steps.after_steps_en: That is the whole process. What takes the time is usually step 2 and step 4, and those are the parts we take on if you would rather not.

S5_correct_documents.en_source_paragraph_1: You need your passport details, your tax file number if you have it, your visa details, each fund's name and ideally its member number or ABN, plus bank details, Australian or overseas. add.q_en: When can I claim my super after leaving Australia?
add.a_en: As soon as both conditions are met: your visa has expired or been cancelled and you have left Australia, with no other Australian visa active. If you left before your visa ran out, Home Affairs can cancel the rest of it once you are overseas. You can start the ATO's online application before you leave and submit it afterwards.

add.q_en: Is there a DASP form, or is it all online?
add.a_en: Both exist. The ATO's DASP online application is free, can search for your accounts if you give your TFN, and creates one application per account, ATO-held super included. The paper form, NAT 7204, is sent to each fund separately and is slower.

add.caution: 'and is slower' is an inference; drop it if the writer prefers to state only facts.

add.q_en: What changes if my super balance is $5,000 or more?
add.a_en: The tax rate does not change. What can change is the paperwork: on a paper application for $5,000 or more you may need a Certification of Immigration Status from the Department of Home Affairs, which has a fee. Any fund may also ask for certified copies of your identity documents, whatever the balance.

add.q_en: Can permanent residents or New Zealand citizens claim a DASP?
add.a_en: No. A DASP is only for former temporary visa holders. Australian and New Zealand citizens and permanent residents cannot claim it. New Zealand citizens may be able to move Australian super to a KiwiSaver scheme instead, under the trans-Tasman transfer rules.

rephrase.existing_en: Why is the DASP rate 65% for working holiday makers and 35% for others?
rephrase.new_q_en: Why is DASP tax so high for working holiday makers?
rephrase.new_a_en: Because the law sets a separate 65% rate for super built up on a 417 or 462 visa, in force since 1 July 2017. If any of your payment comes from contributions made while you held one of those visas, the 65% applies to the whole payment. Other temporary residents pay 35% on the taxed element and 45% on the untaxed element.
rephrase.evidence: why is dasp tax so high 21 pos 8.6; dasp tax rate 23 pos 12.2; super tax working holiday maker 330 pos 16.0

rephrase.existing_en: Does claiming your super affect your tax return or a future Australian visa?
rephrase.new_a_en: It does not go on your Australian tax return, because the 65% withheld is final. Your super accounts close once they are paid out, so if you come back to work you start with a new fund. Questions about a future visa are for the Department of Home Affairs.
rephrase.reason: The current answer asserts that no later visa application turns on it; no official source found.
